prompt:
Migrate classic-laddie's local LLM inference OFF Ollama and ONTO llama.cpp (llama-server) + llama-swap, using the first-class nixpkgs NixOS modules. Motivation: Ollama's custom-ggml vendoring just broke the nightly rebuild (ollama-cuda 0.32.1 failed to compile, blocking the whole generation), and we're moving to the more stable llama.cpp stack. This is a cosmo repo change -> normal PR workflow, follow AGENTS.md.

=== HARD FACTS (already researched on the host - do not re-derive) ===
- Host GPU: single NVIDIA RTX 4090, 24GB VRAM (the docs/classic-laddie-hardware.md doc is STALE and says 3080 Ti/12GB - ignore it; nvidia-smi confirms 4090 24GB). allowUnfree is already set for this GPU host.
- Current inference is services.ollama (pkgs.ollama-cuda) in hosts/classic-laddie/default.nix (~line 449-467), listening on 127.0.0.1:11434, OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192.
- The THREE models to preserve, with their exact underlying model/quant (from the running ollama):
    qwen2.5-coder:32b  -> Qwen2.5-Coder 32B, Q4_K_M GGUF (~19.9GB)
    qwen3:32b          -> Qwen3 32B, Q4_K_M GGUF (~20.2GB)
    gemma4:26b         -> Gemma (family 'gemma4') 25.8B, Q4_K_M GGUF (~18.0GB)
  Source equivalent Q4_K_M GGUFs from Hugging Face (bartowski / unsloth / ggml-org are the usual reliable quant publishers). VERIFY each HF repo/file actually exists before wiring it. For gemma4:26b, confirm the correct Gemma model behind that tag and find a matching GGUF; if no clean Q4_K_M GGUF exists for that exact model, pick the closest current Gemma ~27B Q4_K_M and note the substitution clearly in the PR.
- KEEP THE MODEL IDs IDENTICAL: expose them in llama-swap as 'qwen2.5-coder:32b', 'qwen3:32b', 'gemma4:26b' so open-webui and any caller see the same names.
- VRAM budget: a 32B Q4_K_M (~20GB) + 8192-token KV cache fits in 24GB but ONLY ONE MODEL AT A TIME. Do NOT configure concurrent/multiple-resident models - configure llama-swap to swap (load-on-request, unload the previous), with an idle TTL so VRAM frees when unused. Keep context at 8192 (per-request override possible).

=== ENDPOINT CONTRACT (verified repo-wide) ===
- The ONLY consumer of the local endpoint is services.open-webui (port 8888) in the same file. reel-life uses the Anthropic Claude API (anthropic-sdk-go), NOT local inference. A grep across ALL ~/hack repos for '11434'/'ollama' finds nothing else. So you only need to keep a working local OpenAI-compatible endpoint for open-webui.
- Keep the inference endpoint LOCALHOST-ONLY (127.0.0.1), exactly like ollama was - do NOT expose the inference API on the LAN/firewall. This is a deliberate security boundary.

=== TASKS ===
1. Remove the services.ollama block.
2. Add llama.cpp + llama-swap via the nixpkgs modules. Read their option schemas first:
     nixos/modules/services/networking/llama-swap.nix  (services.llama-swap)
     nixos/modules/services/misc/llama-cpp.nix         (services.llama-cpp)
   Use a CUDA-enabled llama.cpp (e.g. pkgs.llama-cpp.override { cudaSupport = true; }). Configure llama-swap with the three models; each model's command should run llama-server with GPU offload (-ngl 99/999), -c 8192, bound to localhost. Give llama-swap the same 127.0.0.1:11434 (or another localhost port) and make sure it serves the OpenAI API (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/models).
3. Model files: the GGUFs are large (~58GB total) and must NOT go into the nix store. Put them under a systemd StateDirectory (e.g. /var/lib/llama-swap/models) - either via llama-server's built-in -hf auto-download into a persistent HF cache dir, or a small oneshot download service. Pick the clean, reproducible approach and document it.
4. Repoint services.open-webui at the new OpenAI endpoint (e.g. environment = { ENABLE_OLLAMA_API = "False"; OPENAI_API_BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1"; OPENAI_API_KEY = "sk-local"; }). Verify against the current open-webui module option names.
5. Revert the temporary nixpkgs pin: the desired END STATE is nixpkgs.url = "github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable" (with ollama-cuda gone, the frozen channel builds clean again, so the pin added in the ollama-hotfix PR is no longer needed). Reconcile with whatever main currently has - if the pin PR merged, revert it here with a comment; if not, just leave the URL on nixos-unstable.

=== VERIFY (CI is dry-run only and will NOT catch build/runtime failures - you MUST verify on this host) ===
- Build the real toplevel (not --dry-run): nix build .#nixosConfigurations.classic-laddie.config.system.build.toplevel --no-link -L  -- it must complete, including the CUDA llama.cpp.
- Functional smoke test WITHOUT switching the live system (do not nixos-rebuild switch the running host): from the built config or by running the llama-swap + llama-server binaries manually against ONE downloaded GGUF on a scratch localhost port, curl the OpenAI endpoint: GET /v1/models should list the three IDs, and POST /v1/chat/completions with model 'qwen3:32b' should return a completion using the GPU. If feasible, confirm swap behavior (request a second model and confirm the first is unloaded / VRAM freed). Report nvidia-smi before/after.
- Run nix flake check and at least a --dry-run build of the makers-nix and johnny-walker toplevels to confirm nothing else regressed.

=== PR ===
Title e.g. 'feat(classic-laddie): replace Ollama with llama.cpp + llama-swap'. In the body: explain the motivation (ollama vendoring fragility that broke the rebuild), the exact model mappings (and any gemma substitution), that the endpoint stays localhost-only, that open-webui was repointed, that the nixpkgs pin is reverted, and paste the smoke-test evidence (curl output + nvidia-smi). Do NOT switch the live host - the cosmo-rebuild converge loop will roll it out on merge. Keep the change scoped to this migration; do not touch unrelated config.
